study.question: At the strongest validation-selected joint model, does excluding the native auxiliary orthogonal direction from a fixed-carrier shared-context update contribute beyond its retained magnitude, orientation bit and validity gates?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: replacing the auxiliary-derived tangent line by a fixed carrier improved same-seed click AUC (g3-r0051-paired_positive_bridge 0.6683166124 versus g3-r0052-fixed_line_negative 0.6688558745, with external sign also changed); the full line-by-sign controls, not this diagonal comparison, identify differences. In g3-r0053, bit removal increased positive-sign AUC from 0.6685951092 to 0.6686452073 but decreased negative-sign AUC from 0.6688558745 to 0.6683159780. The fixed carrier still excludes native O, so its claimed replacement leaves auxiliary direction information in the feasible subspace. Hypothesis: this exclusion, rather than only native radius and the transported bit, usefully steers the incumbent update. Removing only O exclusion should harm the negative-sign incumbent; the positive-sign cell tests interaction. All are provisional single-seed observations; a generic coordinate-carrier optimization explanation remains plausible.

study.proposed_difference: Add a standalone K-only carrier projection with two FP64 K-removal passes, the same native ||O|| radius, canonical first-max line convention and s(Q) bit. Gate by the inherited fixed-oriented line being nonzero. A 2x2 projection-subspace by external-sign suite executes both geometries in all cells and changes only the selected surrogate VJP. Exact original model and all private gradients at matched state are preserved by source; host checks remain necessary. No claim of a scalar-objective gradient, production causal validity, new forward architecture or verified novelty. Prerequisite audit: current source and DIN hashes match exposed receipts, all 98 exposed trajectory entries are successful executions, and no previous runtime error is pending. Raw parquet/loader re-audit, baseline execution and all tensor checks are unavailable in this proposal-only environment; existing receipts are inherited evidence rather than a new local reproduction. validate_task.py is not a registered authorized reference.
predictions: Primary: click_subspace_negative will have lower full-validation click AUC than aux_subspace_negative_bridge if O exclusion is useful at the incumbent. Report the positive-sign simple contrast and difference of differences without selecting a preferred sign after outcomes.

At identical frozen inputs/state, probabilities, buffers, ordinary scalar loss and private-task parameter gradients should match; only the shared-context cotangent differs. Both transfers should have identical occupied zero support and native norm, be centered and K-orthogonal in FP64. K-only update may overlap O; the bridge should not.

No parameters or inference operations are added; expected parameter count 32192421 and same inference graph. Common extra geometry increases training work in all four arms; measure GPU/wall cost, memory and latency rather than claiming efficiency.
Exact old-branch same-seed bridge AUCs should reproduce 0.6688558744746697 and 0.6685951091914883. Replays establish execution continuity only.

Host preflight must report K-only versus K/O line cosine/angle and relative displacement at matched frozen states, in addition to gate mismatch counts, pivot ties/near ties, transported-bit balance, radius ratios, centered means and K/O inner products before/after the inherited cast. If the two lines barely differ, a null AUC contrast has low mechanistic resolution and does not establish that auxiliary geometry is irrelevant. No custom diagnostic API is assumed; this requirement remains pending under the authorized host evaluation interface.
falsifiers: No reproducible decrease from removing O exclusion at the incumbent, with valid local geometry, falsifies useful O exclusion in this implementation; it does not falsify all auxiliary supervision.
A changed private gradient, forward prediction, buffer update or true-label loss at identical state invalidates the intended intervention.
Any new-only zero/near-degenerate cell or norm mismatch prevents a pure matched-radius exclusion interpretation. Report rather than suppress these cases.

Failure of exact bridges or sensitivity to reduction/pivot ties invalidates attribution until resolved; previously observed FP32/reduction trajectory drift warns against treating code equivalence as empirical parity.
If later authorized independent paired seeds reverse the effect, keep current results as seed-specific and reject repeated-support claims.
alternative_explanations: Arbitrary canonical coordinates, carrier anisotropy, pivot-bit balance or batch ordering can interact with sparse Adagrad independently of informative auxiliary direction.
The retained native radius and bit may carry all useful supervision; exclusion may be unnecessary or harmful.
BF16 cast, repeated categorical IDs and adaptive optimizer state can turn a local row-space projection into a different parameter update; no parameter-space interference conclusion follows.

Multiple validation-selected trajectories and one seed permit selection optimism. There are 98 successful exposed trajectories and no execution failures in the current index; scientific negative branches include rolled labels, FP32 collection and canonical/paired replacements.
The offline benchmark may expose immature historical feedback; auxiliary labels match user/category/brand over 24h rather than ad-specific conversion.

In a high-dimensional context array, a deterministic carrier may already be nearly orthogonal to native O. A small measured angular intervention would make a null outcome weak evidence. No geometry diagnostics were requested in the inherited receipts, so their validity has not been empirically verified.
